evidence: `file -I` on all ten in-scope files returns charset=us-ascii for nine and charset=utf-8 for lib/reader.js (the only file with a non-ASCII byte, the U+2019 at lib/reader.js:730). No other charset appears.

`grep -nP '\t'` and `grep -nP '[\x{00A0}\x{2000}-\x{200B}\x{202F}\x{205F}\x{3000}\x{FEFF}]'` over all ten files return zero hits; a trailing-whitespace grep is also empty. Indentation is two ASCII spaces throughout, e.g. lib/focus/blocks.js:39-45.

`grep` for `\\x`, `\\u` and legacy octal escapes across the ten files returns zero hits. The only backslash escapes in string literals are regex escapes inside the injected-script templates, e.g. lib/reader.js:62 `/Page [0-9,]+ of [0-9,]+[^\\n]{0,20}/`.

The only non-ASCII character in scope is the printable typographic apostrophe at lib/reader.js:730 (`'your own browser’s Amazon session has expired too...'`), written as the literal character, which is what the rule prescribes. No printable character is written as an escape and no non-printable character appears at all.

No file carries an `@fileoverview` tag, which the rule makes optional. Every file opens with a substantive header instead: lib/reader.js:14-39 is a multi-paragraph JSDoc explaining the headless-render design, and lib/focus/blocks.js:1-17, lib/focus/store.js:1-7, lib/video/probe.js:1-5 and lib/latency.js:1-8 each describe content, usage and dependencies rather than restating the filename.

All eight relative imports stay inside lib/: the deepest are `'../../state/system.js'` (lib/focus/breakers/frontmost.js:9) and `'../../video/whitelist.js'` (lib/focus/breakers/video.js:6), both two parent steps and both inside the same package. No import has three or more parent steps and no absolute filesystem path is imported.

No namespace (`import * as`) import exists in scope. The largest named-import list is four symbols (lib/reader.js:4 `import { connect, findBrowser, launchBrowser, requireWebSocket } from './cdp.js'`), well under a dozen. `import fs from 'node:fs'` (lib/reader.js:1) is a Node builtin default import, not a namespace import of a single-export module.

`grep -n 'export default'` over all ten files returns zero hits. Every export is named, e.g. lib/focus/blocks.js:22 `export function localDay`, lib/reader.js:314 `export class Reader`, lib/video/whitelist.js:37 `export function isWhitelisted`.

No `export let` or `export var` exists in scope, and no exported object is mutated after its definition. Exports are `const` or `function`/`class`, e.g. lib/focus/breakers/frontmost.js:15 `export const PANEL_APPS = ['Interstice', 'interstice'];`. Residual note for the reducer: PANEL_APPS and DEFAULT_BLACKLIST (frontmost.js:15,18) are exported arrays that are not `Object.freeze`d, so an importer could mutate their contents even though frontmost.js:7 claims 'a user cannot break it'.

`grep -nE '\bstatic\b'` over all ten files returns zero hits, so no static-member container class exists. The three classes in scope (lib/focus/store.js:15 StarLogError, lib/video/whitelist.js:7 BadVideoURLError, lib/reader.js:314 Reader) all carry instance state and instance methods; module-level constants and functions are exported directly from the module.

The rule has no referent: every in-scope file is plain ES-module JavaScript (package.json declares `"type": "module"` with no TypeScript toolchain), so there are no type positions and no `import type` / `export type` forms to mark. All imports in scope (e.g. lib/reader.js:1-12) are runtime value imports.

`grep` for `namespace X {`, `module X {`, `require(` and triple-slash reference directives across the ten files returns zero hits. Organization is by ES module throughout, e.g. lib/focus/store.js:9-12 uses `import` and lib/focus/store.js:27 `export function open`.

evidence: All three class declarations in scope are unterminated, as required: lib/focus/store.js:15-21 `export class StarLogError extends Error { ... }`, lib/video/whitelist.js:7-12, and lib/reader.js:314-1722 all close with a bare `}`. The rule has no referent: `readonly` is a TypeScript modifier and every in-scope file is plain JavaScript (package.json sets `"type": "module"` with no TypeScript toolchain), so no class field can carry it. lib/reader.js:315-375 declares its fields as plain assignments with no modifier syntax available.

No `public` modifier appears anywhere in scope (JavaScript has none to write), and the project uses exactly one privacy mechanism, the `#` syntax, with no `private` keyword mixed in: lib/reader.js:491 `#runSignIn`, :734 `#evaluate`, :744 `#start`, :774 `#openTab`, :1205 `#shoot`, :1340 `#enqueue`. No field initialisation order across a hierarchy is relied on; the two Error subclasses set their own fields after `super()`.

Every named top-level function in scope is a declaration; `grep -nE '^(export )?const \w+ = (\(|async|function)'` over all ten files returns zero hits. Examples: lib/focus/blocks.js:22,28,38,74; lib/video/whitelist.js:15,37; lib/latency.js:13,17; lib/video/probe.js:11,16,27; lib/reader.js:44,122,142,231,265.

The nested functions in this module's own code are all declarations, hoisted above their use: lib/focus/store.js:31 `function award(blockCompleted)` inside `open()`, lib/video/probe.js:11 `function hostOf(url)`, lib/focus/breakers/frontmost.js:20 `function matches(app, entry)`. Exactly one `function (` expression exists in scope, lib/reader.js:307 `navigator.credentials.get = function (...args) {`, and it is the 'where required' case the rule carves out: it wraps `navigator.credentials.get` and forwards the caller's receiver at :309, which an arrow function cannot do because an arrow would capture the enclosing `this` instead. Every other callback in scope is an arrow, and every named function is a declaration.

Concise-body arrows are used for pure side effects in several places, so a non-void return is silently propagated into a slot that ignores it. lib/reader.js:632 `const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), timeoutMs);` and lib/reader.js:1711 `const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), 4000);` both return `resolve`'s undefined out of a callback whose value is discarded, and lib/reader.js:524 `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1200));` (also :623, :940, :1053, :1142, :1374) returns a Timeout handle out of a Promise executor that ignores it.
fix: Give each side-effect arrow a block body: `setTimeout(() => { resolve(false); }, timeoutMs)` at lib/reader.js:632 and :1711, and `new Promise((r) => { setTimeout(r, 1200); })` at lib/reader.js:524, :623, :940, :1053, :1142 and :1374.

The one `this`-bearing call, lib/reader.js:309 `return real.apply(this, args);`, forwards the receiver the caller supplied through a deliberate `function (...args)` wrapper rather than rebinding it to anything, which is the transparent-forwarding case rather than the rebinding the rule prohibits.

`grep -nw 'arguments'` over all ten files returns zero hits, and the one `.apply(` call, lib/reader.js:309 `return real.apply(this, args);`, already takes its list from the rest parameter declared at :307 `function (...args)`. The rule has no referent: every in-scope file is plain JavaScript with no type annotations, so there is no `type X = { ... }` alias and no `interface` to prefer. evidence: All number literals in scope are decimal with no leading-zero octal and no hexadecimal, so there is no base prefix or hex casing to get wrong: lib/focus/blocks.js:19 `const MS_PER_MINUTE = 60_000;` uses the digit separator where it aids reading, and durations are written as readable products, e.g. lib/reader.js:382 `idleCloseMs: r.idleCloseMs ?? 15 * 60 * 1000`.

lib/video/probe.js uses `!!` for boolean coercion in three places instead of the explicit `Boolean(x)` the rule prescribes: line 19 `playing: !!r.playing`, line 46 `playing = !!res?.result?.value;`, and line 50 `readerProfile: !!b.readerProfile`. The codebase's own convention elsewhere is the explicit form, e.g. lib/reader.js:94 `painted: Boolean(label || loc) || ...`, :405 `return Boolean(this.cdp && !this.cdp.closed && this.browser);` and :1098 `ready: Boolean(probe.painted)`.
fix: Replace the three `!!` coercions in lib/video/probe.js with `Boolean(...)`: line 19 `playing: Boolean(r.playing)`, line 46 `playing = Boolean(res?.result?.value);`, line 50 `readerProfile: Boolean(b.readerProfile)`.

evidence: Three brace-less `if` statements in lib/reader.js carry an `else`, which the rule's one-line exception explicitly does not cover: lines 985-986 `if (!this.running) await this.#start();` / `else if (resized) {`; lines 1066-1067 `if (!paintedAt) paintedAt = Date.now();` / `else if (Date.now() - paintedAt > graceMs) return last;`; and lines 1646-1647 `if (landed) this.#show(landed);` / `else await this.capture({ force: true });`. Every other brace-less body in scope is a single-line `if` with no else, which is permitted.
fix: Brace the `if` bodies at lib/reader.js:985, :1066 and :1646, e.g. `if (!this.running) { await this.#start(); } else if (resized) { ... }` and `if (landed) { this.#show(landed); } else { await this.capture({ force: true }); }`.

evidence: No expression in scope mixes `&&` with `||`, or `??` with either, without grouping. The one mixed-operator expression is fully parenthesised: lib/reader.js:970-974 `wanted && (!this.requested || Math.abs(...) > 8 || Math.abs(...) > 8)`. `??` is likewise always grouped or isolated, e.g. lib/reader.js:1558 `codes[key] ?? (text ? text.charCodeAt(0) : 0)`, :1468 `Date.now() - (this.readAheadFailedAt ?? 0) < 5000`, :1639 `(this.stuck ?? 0) >= 2 && (await this.revive())`. No bit operation appears in scope.

Every `throw` in scope is an Error subclass (lib/focus/store.js:64,67 StarLogError; lib/video/whitelist.js:20,22 BadVideoURLError; lib/reader.js:496,747 Error with a Remedy clause), but errors are discarded with no record at eleven `.catch(() => {})` sites, which is an empty catch by another name and defeats the rule's own carveout wording ('MUST catch, log, and continue'). The undocumented ones: lib/reader.js:843 `await this.#evaluate(CSS_INJECT).catch(() => {});`, :1013 and :1021 `await this.#seed().catch(() => {});`, and :1206 `if (!this.clip) await this.#probe().catch(() => {});` all swallow any failure with neither a log line nor a comment.
fix: At lib/reader.js:843, :1013, :1021 and :1206 replace `.catch(() => {})` with a logging handler, e.g. `.catch((err) => this.logger?.warn?.(`reader: seeding the shelf failed (${err.message})`))`, matching the pattern the file already uses at :837 and :1500.

evidence: The single switch in scope, lib/focus/blocks.js:40-70, has a `default:` at :68 that returns `{ state, emit }`, and every case ends in a `return`: `'start'` at :44, `'tick'` at :58 and :60, `'break'` at :66. No case falls through, so there is no unmarked fallthrough to flag.

`grep -nE '[^=!<>]==[^=]|[^!]!=[^=]'` over all ten files returns zero hits, so no loose equality is used anywhere in scope, not even the permitted `x == null` idiom. Comparisons are strict throughout, e.g. lib/latency.js:34 `if (submittedAt === undefined) return null;`, lib/focus/blocks.js:47 `if (state.phase !== 'running')`, lib/reader.js:1286 `if (this.frontier !== this.pos)`.

The rule has no referent: these are plain .js files with no TypeScript, so no `x as Foo` type assertion and no `x!` non-null assertion can exist; `grep -nE ' as [A-Z]| as const'` returns zero hits. Narrowing is done with runtime guards instead, e.g. lib/reader.js:1120 `if (probe?.clip) this.clip = probe.clip;` and lib/focus/store.js:66 `typeof obj.startedAt !== 'string'`.

Two try blocks in lib/reader.js run far past five statements and end in a catch that cannot tell which of them failed. lib/reader.js:984-1030 (`ensure`) wraps roughly fifteen statements, including `#start`, `#applyViewport`, `settle`, `Page.navigate`, `#evaluate`, `recoverIfPossible` and `#seed`, under one `catch (err) { this.error = err.message; ... }`. lib/reader.js:823-851 (`revive`) wraps ten, including `Target.closeTarget`, `#openTab`, `clearSiteData`, `Page.navigate`, `settle` and `#seed`, under `catch (err) { this.error = err.message; return false; }` at :848-850, so any one of six distinct network or CDP failures reports as the same opaque `false`.
fix: Narrow both try blocks to the call whose failure the catch is written for. In `revive` (lib/reader.js:823-851), wrap only the `Page.navigate`/`settle` pair and let `#openTab` and `#seed` report their own failures; in `ensure` (lib/reader.js:984-1030), split the start path, the navigate-to-book path and the resize path into separate try blocks so `this.error` names the step that failed.

evidence: The rule has no referent: `grep -nE '^\s*@[A-Za-z]'` over all ten in-scope files returns zero hits, so no decorator of any kind is applied. The `@param`/`@returns` tags at lib/focus/blocks.js:33-37 and lib/focus/store.js:24-25 are JSDoc annotations inside comment blocks, not decorators.
